# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - Precious metals prices fell lower in the second half of November. Concerns over the Euro debt crisis kept the pressure on the Euro itself, providing a headwind for all commodities. Underperforming stock markets drove selling of a range of commodities and fears of an economic slowdown weighed on the more industrial of the precious metals. Gold fell nearly $100 to its current level of roughly $1,715 but the other metals found less support from investors and from physical purchasers. With the market concentrating almost entirely on the Euro issue, it may be challenging for metal prices to gain ground in the coming weeks. • All four of the precious metals saw reductions in net long speculative positioning on COMEX/NYMEX in the week to the 22nd of November. In part this may have been due to the forthcoming Thanksgiving celebrations in the USA, with investors keen to reduce their exposure before that festival. However, price decreases also drove long liquidation and the addition of extra short positioning. Platinum suffered least form this selling but silver and palladium fell firmly out of fashion. • In the ETF sector, there was another week of safe haven buying of gold as the Euro debt crisis deepened. For the other three metals, investors were notably less bullish and ETF positions were reduced after small amounts of net selling. ##### **David Jollie** **david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **29 November 2011** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **29 November 2011** ### **Gold CFTC data to 22 November 2011; ETF data to 25 November 2011.** |**Exchang**|**e (COMEX a**

Gold started at $1,780 on the 15th and slipped to $1,760 before crashing to $1,720 on the 17th as the ratings agencies warned of possible contagion of US banks from Europe. Worries that the EFSF would not rescue Italy led to bond yields in the peripheral European nations widening dramatically and a sell-off in equities. Gold made a feeble attempt to move higher, reaching $1,735 on the 18th before slumping to $1,672 on the 21st under selling pressure as investors looked to cover losses elsewhere. Safe haven buying was still seen, though, and gold moved higher off the lows ahead of Thanksgiving, bouncing to $1,710 on the 23rd. It is currently trading a little above that level. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—November 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- As gold tumbled back below $1,700, futures and options investors turned more bearish, selling off their positions ahead of options expiry and Thanksgiving. Net long speculative COMEX positions dropped by 3.84 million ounces to 21.18 million ounces. Open interest decreased a little but the major changes were a decrease in large options positioning and a rise in the number of short futures contracts held by smaller investors. With much of the selling done, the price could be more robust in the coming weeks. TOCOM investors were net buyers, adding 37,000 ounces to their positions. - For the seventh successive week, gold ETF holdings climbed, rising by 212,000 ounces to a global total of 70.2 million ounces, a new record level. The investor response to the current phase of the Eurozone crisis has been the logical one of buying gold. However, buying has been less intense than it was in July, suggesting that risk fatigue may be setting in amongst investors. 2

- Silver suffered the same selling and weak price performance as gold in the second half of November but with the gold:silver ratio increasing as gold asserted its safe haven credentials rather more. Silver traded in its customary wide range, moving from above $34.50 on the 16th to just above $31 on the 17th. Any price recoveries proved to be a little disappointing and ineffectual and silver dipped to a low of under $31 on the 21st. With the selling having abated, investors managed to propel silver to $33 on the 22nd but with physical demand soft and Euro headlines still dominating the market’s thoughts, silver was unable to hold this level and weakened, falling below $32 on the 23rd. Since that point, it has mainly traded in a relatively narrow range from $31 to $32. - Net long speculative interest in silver on COMEX crashed 31.4 million ounces lower in the week to the 22nd of November. This was the largest weekly decrease since late September and the wild swings in investor positioning illustrate the rapidly changing sentiment in the markets. Total positioning now stands at 133.3 million ounces, a little above its lowest level for th

e year. - Silver ETF investors were net sellers for the third week in a row leading up to the 25th of November. They sold 2.7 million ounces more than they bought, with global holdings falling to 456.7 million ounces. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **29 November 2011** ### **Platinum CFTC data to 22 November 2011; ETF data to 25 November 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**||||**TOCOM**|**Net total**|**Price**| |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| |||_Futures_

- Platinum fell $100 from mid-November as investors worried about the twin impacts of a troubled Euro and the possibility of recession in Europe and possibly in other developed economies. Despite gold falling too, the gold-platinum spread widened, suggesting that risk aversion was still the theme for many investors. Information from the Johnson Matthey Platinum Interim Review suggested that the platinum market is in surplus this year and is likely to remain in surplus next year, adding little physical support to the price. However, investors continue to see price support from increasing production costs, allowing them to remain bullish. Platinum started at roughly $1,640 on the 15th and slid downwards to a low of around $1,530 on the 25th with little positive sentiment in evidence. The sharpest price falls came on the 17th and 21st when Euro-related headlines and widening bond spreads scared the equity markets, with metals being sold to cover losses elsewhere. - Although platinum invest

ors added to their short holdings in the week to the 22nd of November, they were less spooked than either silver or palladium investors. On NYMEX, net long speculative positions decreased by 58,000 ounces to 1.18 million ounces. With the direction of the gold price somewhat uncertain, investors are unconvinced as to whether they should add to or reduce their bets on the platinum price. TOCOM investors added cautiously to their holdings for a second week although positioning here remains low. - Although a net 4,300 ounces of platinum were sold by ETF investors in the week to the 25th of November, the selling seen in previous weeks seems to have slowed. Holdings now stand at 1.48 million ounces, a similar level to where they were one month earlier. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **29 November 2011** ### **Palladium CFTC data to 22 November 2011; ETF data to 25 November 2011.** ## **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

The days of $800 plus prices of early 2011 seem a long time ago now. As with platinum, palladium simply slid lower from the 15th onwards as Europe’s debt crisis kept the market’s attention. Every rising bond yield within Europe sparked further selling and palladium lost ground. It fell from $660 on the 15th and found the slightest touch of support at $650 on the 17th before moving lower again to touch $605 that day over worries that the EFSF would not bail out Italy despite pressure from the bond markets and the formation of a new austerity-minded government there. $600 provided some psychological support but investor selling of futures and of ETF metal outweighed some gentle bargain-hunting by end users. The price slipped through that level late on the 18th of November and dropped to $585 on the 21st. Palladium did bounce back over $600 on the 22nd but recorded a new low of $567 on the 25th. Another move higher on the 28th failed to break $600 and the mood is now increasingly bearish. We remain bullish for the palladium price in the longer term but the short t

- After three weeks of growth, net long speculative palladium positions on NYMEX crashed 184,000 ounces lower to 585,000 ounces in the week to the 22nd of November. This is the lowest level of investor exposure since Q1 2009 and illustrates the U- turn in sentiment over palladium in the short term. - The week to the 25th of November saw further selling of palladium by ETF investors. As shown in the graph to the right, the selling has been constant and heavy for most of this year. It is hard to see at what point the selling pressure might stop but we feel a sharp upwards move in the price would spark further buying. 5 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** #### **Disclaimer:** This briefing is for our clients’ information purpose only.
